statement: Each quantity in the paper comes from one data set only; the project's decisions name which set serves which quantity.
why: Mixing data sets makes numbers disagree.
provenance: user ruling 2026-11-17 (tools named; one data set per quantity), generalised

statement: Every result number in the prose is computed from the data by an expression in the project's numbers.tsv and typeset with \val{id}; a registry value that no longer matches its expression, or a hand-typed number equal to a registry value, is an error.
why: Hand-copied numbers drift from the data; the registry is the one source.
provenance: user ruling 2026-11-22; merged data.number-registry + data.no-hand-typed-number (user review 2026-11-23 P2-G6)

statement: Results and figures are generated by scripts archived with the project together with a snapshot of their input data (figures listed in the project's figures.tsv; a figure changes only by editing and re-running its script); the paper states every parameter needed to repeat a simulation (inputs, step, solver settings, sample count) in the method or a table.
why: Results must be reproducible; a figure without its script cannot be regenerated.
provenance: P23 (S1, S4); writing.md#14; merged figure.scripted (user review 2026-11-23 P2-G6)

statement: When two models, methods or data sets differ, write "discrepancy" or "difference"; keep "error" only where a reference truth exists (measurement, analytical exact value).
why: Error claims a truth the comparison lacks.
good: the discrepancy between the two models
bad: the error of the analytical model against FEA
provenance: user ruling 2026-11-17; field weak patterns (EMD, PED)

statement: Agreement, changes and key results are given as numbers: agreement between model and reference as a discrepancy bound, a percent change with its baseline, a small change by its size ("changes by less than 2 %"); never vague words such as "agree well", "clearly", "nearly" or "hardly changes".
why: Numbers are checkable; vague words are not evidence.
bad: hardly changes; clearly lower; nearly all
provenance: field weak patterns (PED, EMD); user rulings 2026-11-12, writing.md#28; merged data.quantified-agreement + author.numbers-are-specific + author.size-of-small-change (user review 2026-11-23 P2-G6)

statement: A number and its unit are separated by a thin space (\,), never a plain space or nothing; a degree sign or a prime follows its number with no space.
why: SI typesetting; a plain space can break the line between number and unit.
provenance: new (corpus slip: space before a degree sign); examples paraphrase; original withheld until publication
